name: System analytics (data surfaces)
note: Phase 6 (kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Chart tokens): the four chart tick formats the Phase 5 hand-off names (chartXAxis.ts:50, :80, :85, :91), each chart's range line (the unit, the bucket and the period, under the chart's title), the text summary of each chart (the figure's caption and accessible description), the KPI tiles' third line (the baseline, or that there is none) and the token table's unit header. When a chart's series is empty the empty-state line of Phase 5 (A-03.21, A-03.26, A-03.28) is the figure's whole text and no summary is drawn. The six preset rows give `{range}` its sentence form, and the bracketed-dates row gives a preset's range line its dates; every summary writes the period after "for", which reads the same for a preset, a custom range and a single day. Every donut slice carries its name as a direct label, and User duration is in hours throughout. Two format rows supersede a Phase 5 row at one line each: A-03.52 at the table cell and A-03.22 at the User duration legend.

rows.t: The daily X-axis tick (`formatAnalyticsDateTick`, chartXAxis.ts:50): day first and the month from the fixed table, with no locale argument. The year is left out because the chart's range line states it, which `§ Dates, times and numbers` allows for a tick where the axis names the year.
The hourly axis's midnight tick (`formatAnalyticsTimeTick`, chartXAxis.ts:80): the date, written as the daily tick is; the other hours read HH:mm.
The hourly tick (chartXAxis.ts:85): HH:mm on the 24-hour clock, the minutes always written (the old form drew `2pm` and `2:05pm`).
The chart tooltip's time (`formatAnalyticsTimeTooltip`, chartXAxis.ts:91): the full date and time, one format (C3).

The tile's third line is its baseline or trend (`§ Chart tokens › KPI tiles`). The analytics API returns the chosen range only, so there is no earlier period to compare, and the line says so instead of implying one (C16). The description it replaces repeated the label (C6).
The Sessions tile's third line: no earlier period in the data, so none is claimed (C16); the old description repeated the label (C6).
The Interactions tile's third line: no earlier period in the data (C16); the old description repeated the label (C6).
The Average session tile's third line: no earlier period in the data (C16). The label already says average and the value carries the unit (`{n} min`, A-03.22), so the description is not needed (C6).

The chart's second line states the unit, the bucket and the period (`§ Chart tokens › Encoding rules`): `{range}` is a custom range as its dates (A-03.43, `D MMM – D MMM YYYY`; a single day as its date, `D MMM YYYY`) or a preset in its sentence form (the preset rows of this group) with its dates in brackets after it (the bracketed-dates row of this group), so the line always states its days and its year, which the X ticks leave out ("Users per hour, 17 Oct 2026"; "Users per hour, the last 24 hours (6 Oct – 7 Oct 2026)"). The hourly reading of the template at StandaloneUserActivity.tsx:121; the next row is the daily one.

The daily reading of the template at StandaloneUserActivity.tsx:121 (the previous row is the hourly one); `{range}` as in the previous row: "Users per day, the last 7 days (1 Oct – 7 Oct 2026)" for a preset, "Users per day, 1 Oct – 7 Oct 2026" for a custom range.

The sessions chart's second line, the hourly reading of the template at StandaloneDailySessions.tsx:121: `{range}` is a custom range as its dates (A-03.43, `D MMM – D MMM YYYY`; a single day as its date, `D MMM YYYY`) or a preset in its sentence form (the preset rows of this group) with its dates in brackets after it (the bracketed-dates row of this group), so the line always states its days and its year, which the X ticks leave out ("Sessions per hour, 17 Oct 2026").
The daily reading of the same template (StandaloneDailySessions.tsx:121); `{range}` as in the previous row.

The Top actions chart's second line: the unit (interactions), the grouping and the period; `{range}` is a custom range as its dates (A-03.43, `D MMM – D MMM YYYY`; a single day as its date, `D MMM YYYY`) or a preset in its sentence form (the preset rows of this group) with its dates in brackets after it (the bracketed-dates row of this group), so the line always states its days and its year, which the X ticks leave out.

The User duration chart's second line gains the period (`{range}` as in the rows above: a custom range as its dates, a preset with its dates in brackets); "Estimated" stays, because the minutes are an estimate (chat actions × 2 and code actions × 5, StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:48-55) and the chart may not claim a measurement (C16).
The Model choice chart's second line: the unit the legend already uses (requests, A-03.53), the grouping and the period (C3; `{range}` as in the rows above); "usage" and "distribution" went (C6).

The User duration legend's second activity (StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:63) is the student code page, which the interface calls the scratchpad (`§ Terminology`; A-03.16 already drops IDE from Code runs).

The Token usage detail table's fourth column (StandaloneTopTokenUsers.tsx:458) counts interactions, as its cells say (A-03.52); the header names the unit (C6; `§ Chart tokens › Tables`). The Tokens header already does.

rows.at: src/components/Analytics/StandaloneUserActivity.tsx:134 (the figure's caption and accessible description; new text)
rows.t: The text summary of the hourly active-users chart (`§ Chart tokens › Text summaries`): the key figure first, the period stated, then the peak, all computed from the drawn series (StandaloneUserActivity.tsx:134); no trend claim the data cannot back (C16). The period follows "for", which reads with every form of `{range}` ("for the last 24 hours", "for 6 Oct – 7 Oct 2026", "for 17 Oct 2026", where "in 17 Oct 2026" would not), so one template serves a preset, a custom range and a single day; a preset's dates are on the range line above the plot and are not repeated here. `{total}` is the range's unique users (the Active users tile): "different users", because a user active on several days counts once and the figure is not the sum of the bars, `{peak}` the largest bucket and `{peakAt}` its start.

rows.at: src/components/Analytics/StandaloneUserActivity.tsx:121 (after a preset's sentence form in each chart's range line; new text)
rows.t: A preset's range line gives the preset's dates in brackets after its sentence form ("Users per day, the last 7 days (1 Oct – 7 Oct 2026)"): the X ticks leave the year out because the range line states it, and a relative period alone states neither the days nor the year once the page is shared or printed (`§ Chart tokens › Encoding rules`). `{dates}` is the preset's first and last day in the range format of A-03.43 (`D MMM – D MMM YYYY`, the year written twice when the years differ: "the last 12 months (7 Oct 2025 – 7 Oct 2026)"); the last 24 hours give their two calendar days ("6 Oct – 7 Oct 2026"). Every range line on the page takes it (StandaloneUserActivity.tsx:121, StandaloneDailySessions.tsx:121, StandaloneTopActions.tsx:183, StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:175, StandaloneUserEngine.tsx:145); a custom range is already its dates and adds nothing, and the summaries do not repeat them.

rows.at: src/components/Analytics/StandaloneUserEngine.tsx:166 (each slice's direct label; new text)
rows.t: Each donut slice's direct label (`§ Chart tokens › Encoding rules › Donuts`): its name as the legend writes it (ChatGPT, Qwen, Unknown, A-03.24 and A-03.25; Chat and Scratchpad, P6-A-03.16) over its share, a whole percent, outside the ring beside the slice and joined to a thin slice by a leader. It names every slice in words, so no slice is told by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1): under colour-vision simulation ChatGPT (`--chart-1`) and Unknown (`--chart-other`) are only 4.66 apart (light, protanopia). The User duration donut takes the same label (StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:207); the shares leave the legends, which keep the values with their units.

Supersedes A-03.22's New at this line only (the User duration legend's value, StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:304): the chart has one unit, the hour (`§ Chart tokens › Encoding rules › Donuts`), so the legend gives each activity's estimate in hours, to two significant figures like the centre, where it gave minutes beside a centre in hours. It says about, as the summary does: the hours are rounded from an estimate whose minutes also give the shares, so "about 20 hours" (62%) and "about 13 hours" (38%) agree with "33 hours" within the rounding, where bare figures would not (20 of 33 is 61%). It begins lowercase because it follows the activity's name in the legend ("Chat about 20 hours") and never stands alone (C1): the written exemption covers the lowercase start. Its share moves to the slice's direct label (the slice-label row).

The User duration figure in hours, to two significant figures ("33" for 32.9 hours, "4.5", "0.33": never more digits, and never 0 for a part that is not 0), in place of one decimal ("32.9"), which claims a precision the estimate does not have (C16: the minutes are action counts times 2 and 5, StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:48-51). Two sites: the centre total (StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:130, drawn over its noun, "hours", or "hour" when the figure is 1) and the tooltip's figure (StandaloneUserDuration.tsx:117, which A-03.49 writes as "Duration: {hours: count hour}"). The legend (the row above) and the summary (P6-A-03.23) read the same figure.

name: Class analytics (data surfaces)
note: Phase 6 (kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Chart tokens): the KPI tiles' third line (the Questions tile's week-on-week trend, one row per direction, the denominator where the value is a ratio, or that there is no earlier period), the intent chart's direct label (its share: the chart draws no value axis) and its bars' tooltip (the count), and the text summaries of the intent chart and the topic bars, each in its unscoped and its lecture-scoped reading. The four scope lines state what each chart covers, because the page has no date range.

rows.n: Last full week: {m: count question}, up from {previous} the week before
rows.at: src/components/ClassAnalytics/ClassAnalytics.tsx:429 (the Questions tile's third line; new text)
rows.t: The Questions tile's third line (`§ Chart tokens › KPI tiles`): a week-on-week trend from the weekly series the page already fetches and never draws (`weeklyActivity`, classAnalyticsApi.ts:20), so the tile carries a trend and not just context. This reading shows when the last full week had more questions than the week before (`{m}` > `{previous}`); the other directions are P6-A-18.17 (down) and P6-A-18.18 (the same). The weeks are the backend's UTC Mondays (`date_trunc('week')` over the class's chat questions, ../kiwi/src/analytics/class-analytics.service.ts:177-183, sent as the UTC instant of Monday 00:00 by `toISOString()`): the last full week is the latest Monday-to-Sunday week that has ended in UTC, and the week before is the Monday seven days earlier; a week missing from the series counts as 0, because the GROUP BY returns no row for a week without questions. The comparison is drawn only when the week before falls on or after the series' first week; otherwise, with an empty series, and while a lecture is chosen (the value is then that lecture's count and the series the whole class's), the line is "No earlier period to compare" (the tile rows below). The line takes the Phase 3 tile's direction glyph in its own colour (`--kpi-tile-trend`), hidden from assistive technology: the words state the direction, so neither the glyph nor a colour carries it. No percentage: a change between small counts reads larger than it is, and a week from 0 has none.
